**Yes — the documents contradict each other on remote work in three distinct areas.** The contradiction scanner reports 8 flags in total, and the remote-work ones are verified and still open (none resolved or dismissed).

## 1. How many remote days per week — three incompatible numbers

| Rule | Source |
|---|---|
| Up to **5 days/week**, "no mandatory office attendance day" | [ui_check_remote_policy § Remote Work Policy (2026 Revision)] |
| Maximum **1 day/week**; at least 4 office days per calendar week | [remote_work_policy_v2 § 2. Office Attendance] |
| Up to **3 days/week**; remaining days at the assigned office | [remote_work_policy_v1 § 2. Remote Work Allowance] |

The scanner flags the 5-day rule as incompatible with the 1-day cap (flag #11, confidence 0.99) and with the 3-day cap (flag #10, confidence 0.98). The 1-day and 3-day rules are also mutually exclusive on their face — 1 ≠ 3 — though the scanner's flags pair each of them against the 5-day version rather than against each other.

## 2. Home-office / equipment allowance — different amounts and currencies

- One-time equipment budget of **$600**, with tiers of $400 / $600 / $800 [sample_policy (3) § Policy Number: RW-2025-014. Effective Date: March 1, 2025.]
- One-time home-office allowance of **INR 25,000** [ui_check_remote_policy § Remote Work Policy (2026 Revision)]

Flag #13 (confidence 0.82) records these as incompatible entitlement amounts/currencies for the same benefit. Note the scanner explicitly says the *remote-days* rules in these two passages are **not** contradictory — the sample policy's tier table also tops out at 5 days/week.

## 3. Internet stipend — fixed stipend vs. capped reimbursement

- **$50/month** stipend for anyone remote ≥3 days/week, paid through payroll, **no receipts required**; tier amounts $50 / $60 / $75 [sample_policy (3) § Policy Number: RW-2025-014. Effective Date: March 1, 2025.]
- Home internet reimbursed **up to $60/month**, must be the primary connection, with an itemized receipt [expense_policy § 2. Reimbursable Categories]

Flag #12 (confidence 0.97) records these as incompatible rules for the same benefit — and notes the Gold tier's $75 exceeds the $60 cap.

## What the documents do *not* resolve

None of the passages states which version supersedes which, and I found no precedence or "this policy replaces" clause in the remote-work documents. The dates are: v1 effective 2024-01-01 [remote_work_policy_v1 § 2. Remote Work Allowance], v2 effective 2025-06-01 [remote_work_policy_v2 § 2. Office Attendance], and the 5-day version labelled a "2026 Revision" [ui_check_remote_policy § Remote Work Policy (2026 Revision)] — but the documents themselves do not say the later-dated one governs. That determination needs People Operations.

**One thing that is *not* a conflict:** the sample policy RW-2025-014 appears three times in the corpus as `sample_policy`, `sample_policy (2)` and `sample_policy (3)`, with identical text [sample_policy § Policy Number: RW-2025-014. Effective Date: March 1, 2025.; sample_policy (2) § Policy Number: RW-2025-014. Effective Date: March 1, 2025.; sample_policy (3) § Policy Number: RW-2025-014. Effective Date: March 1, 2025.]. That is duplication, not disagreement.

- [remote_work_policy_v2 § 2. Office Attendance]
- [remote_work_policy_v1 § 2. Remote Work Allowance]
- [sample_policy (3) § Policy Number: RW-2025-014. Effective Date: March 1, 2025.]
- [expense_policy § 2. Reimbursable Categories]
